name: Laguna Fabrics
old_description: Since 2000, Laguna has been making fabric with raw materials that have a lower environmental impact than conventional materials and today we are doing even more.
about:
Laguna Fabrics was founded in 1986 in Los Angeles, California, by Monet Goode and has been operated by the Roshan family across multiple generations. The company began as a circular knitting mill serving the contemporary fashion market and has remained a family-owned business for nearly 35 years.

The mill runs in-house circular knitting machines from low to fine gauge, with a capacity of 1.5 million pounds per month, and offers special finishes such as brushing and sueding along with fabric laundering. With 40 employees, Laguna produces over 10 million yards annually, focusing on certified sustainable fibers including GOTS organic cotton, TENCEL™ lyocell, TENCEL™ modal, recycled cotton, and hemp. Services include technical fabric analysis, new construction engineering, on-trend fabric development, on-demand sample yardage, and a showroom with a complete lab-dip catalog.

Laguna supplies trend-forward knits to contemporary fashion brands, independent designers, and start-up labels, emphasizing quick turnaround enabled by domestic production. Longtime clients receive dedicated service, while the company also supports younger designers and smaller ventures with low minimums and development assistance.

The company’s differentiation rests on its GOTS certification—it claims to be the only circular knit mill in the United States with that credential—and a commitment to provenance, process transparency, and product authenticity. Since 2000 it has shifted toward lower-impact materials, joining the Textile Exchange and the California Cotton & Climate Coalition, with a stated goal of reaching 90 percent sustainable material output by 2025.
